title: Fast-method verification evidence
description: Evidence that a fast method was checked (SESSION 009 / SPEC-PYQ-002). A VERIFIED_FAST_METHOD may only exist if such a record is present with result PASS AND the check was real — deterministic computation over many inputs and edge cases, or a different provider, or a source document. A model's own confidence is not verification. Validated by hand-written checks in tests/pyq/test_pyq_intelligence.py (D-0006).

method_id.description: The fast method being verified. Must resolve to a method whose state is VERIFIED_FAST_METHOD.

approach.description: How the check was done. INDEPENDENT_MODEL requires a verifier provider different from the analyser (no self-verification).

procedure.description: What was checked, in exact terms.

mismatches.description: Count of inputs where the fast result differed from the standard result. Must be 0 for PASS.

variants_tested.description: The input families the fast method was run against (e.g. 'integer percentages', 'fractional ratios'). Not a single example.

edge_cases_tested.description: The edge cases where a shortcut is expected to break (zero, negatives, boundary, degenerate). These are required, not optional.

verified_by.description: Who ran the check. For DETERMINISTIC, the script identity; for INDEPENDENT_MODEL, a verifier provider that differs from the analyser.

evidence.description: Path to or description of the runnable/run output that produced the result.

invariants: result == PASS  =>  standard_vs_fast_equivalence.fast_matches_standard is true AND mismatches == 0
approach == INDEPENDENT_MODEL  =>  verified_by names a provider different from the analyser (a model may not verify its own output)
variants_tested and edge_cases_tested must each contain at least one entry; a claim of verification against a single input is not verification
a verification record never upgrades the underlying question's T2 tier
